title: Machine learning predicts early diabetic kidney disease in a retrospective hospital cohort
summary: Researchers evaluated six survival models in 1,006 patients with type 2 diabetes from one hospital. XGBoost using nine predictors, including the atherogenic index of plasma, achieved one-, three- and five-year AUCs of 0.784, 0.761 and 0.752 in 302 randomly held-out patients. This was internal retrospective validation. Missing values were imputed before splitting, creating possible leakage; clinical benefit was not tested.
ai_technology: XGBoost survival prediction; Boruta and LASSO feature selection
organization: Lanzhou University Second Hospital; Lanzhou University

evidence.tested: Six survival algorithms were compared using 704 training and 302 validation patients; 404 kidney-disease events occurred.
evidence.unknown: External transport, prospective performance and clinical benefit remain unestablished. Pre-split imputation can bias evaluation; the separate AIP association does not establish causation.
evidence.ai_role: XGBoost learned risk from nine baseline predictors; AIP feature importance was assessed using Boruta.

source_review.scope: Publisher Methods, Results, limitations and publication history; supplement and underlying patient data not reviewed.
